messages:
maya: Heads-up — I'm seeing a read-error ripple on local NVMe in ap-south1 that’s causing GPU attach queue to back up. p99 read latency to local scratch jumped from 8ms -> 1200ms for a few hosts. Anyone already digging?

sam: yep noticed similar on the dashboard, started ~09:12 UTC. Attach failures rate up and a couple of rolls moved jobs to pending. logs look like transient read retries, not full device loss.

ops-bot: Alert: nvme-read-retry-rate spike (ap-south1) — 18 hosts above threshold. Incident ID: INC-20260315-AP1-NVME.

anika: can we throttle janitor/scrub concurrency to reduce foreground IO? metrics show scrub throughput spiking around the same time windows.

maya: good call. scrub concurrency on the hot cohort is at 64. proposing to reduce to 16 for next 30m and see. This will increase scrub completion time but should free IO for attaches.

leo: +1. Also suggest temporary scheduling rule: route new GPU provisioning requests away from ap-south1 to eu-west2/us-west1 until we stabilize.

sam: pushed a canary policy to divert new batch launches: added region-affinity override for ephemeral provisioning via the fleet router. Should take effect in ~2m.

maya: copying relevant log snippet from one affected host: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:13:21Z] nvme0n1: read error, retrying (retry_count=3)
[2026-03-15T09:13:21Z] blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1, sector 1234567
[2026-03-15T09:13:21Z] nvme: ctrl 0000:3b:00.0: Completed async event: Read Error
```

kai: interesting — this looks like elevated read-retry counts, firmware not resetting to readonly. Could be thermal or a localized wear hotspot. Are SMART counters showing > threshold?

sam: SMART: increased media_err_count and read_retry in the last 48h on the same cohort. I can run a deeper SMART export.

anika: from an ops perspective, immediate mitigations: 
- reduce janitor/scrub concurrency to 16 (maya)
- temporarily reduce aggressive prefetch on serving nodes (patched via runtime flag)
- divert new provisioning (leo/sam)

maya: doing scrub concurrency bump now: `./opsctl storage tune --cohort hot --scrub-concurrency 16 --reason "read-retry spike"`

ops-bot: Command executed: opsctl storage tune (user: maya) — queued.

leo: I’ll update the routing rule and monitor attach success. If attaches still fail we may need to mark the worst hosts as "degraded" and let them drain. That costs capacity.

sam: while scrub is throttling, I'm going to schedule a micro firmware bump for one repro host to see if read-retry behavior improves. Planning to coordinate with HW team — risk: host reboot.

maya: agree. let's pick a single repro node (host-apse1-78) for the firmware test. If it clears, we can roll. If not, we should consider proactive retire for the small cohort.

kai: cost note: diverting provisioning adds inter-region egress + slightly higher latency for build/test jobs. ops estimate: ~6% monthly cost impact if we keep divert for 48h for affected queues. Lean on product if we need to extend.

anika: capture steps for postmortem: timeline, scrub tuning decision, firmware test outcome, host retire plan, cost delta estimate. Assigning owner: maya.

maya: acknowledged. I’ll be owner and will post an initial incident summary after the firmware test.

sam: running `smartctl -a /dev/nvme0n1 > /tmp/smart-host78.txt` now and uploading to the incident doc.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260315-AP1-NVME updated: scrub concurrency reduced; routing diversion active; firmware test scheduled for host-apse1-78 in 15m.

leo: quick check — any kernel oops or IO scheduler messages? If CFQ/kyber stuck we should switch to noop for scratch.

maya: no kernel oops so far. switch to noop is low-risk; we can flip on affected nodes and measure. Doing that on the repro host post-firmware test: `echo noop > /sys/block/nvme0n1/queue/scheduler`

kai: good. If noop helps, we can template the change across the degraded pool. Remember to revert after we have a long-term fix.

anika: all set for now. monitoring p99 read latency and attach queue length. if anyone sees degradation elsewhere, tag #eng-oncall.

maya: thanks all — will update after the firmware test.

sam: update (10:01 UTC): firmware test applied to host-apse1-78, host rebooted, SMART counters stabilized for that host. p99 read latency down from 1200ms -> 22ms on that host. Testing more nodes in the cohort now.

leo: excellent. next steps: define a paced firmware rollout for the cohort, target 5% hosts/hour, keep scrub concurrency at 16 until rollout completes.

maya: noted. I'll draft the rollout schedule and cost impact calc, and post the incident summary shortly.

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260315-AP1-NVME resolved (provisional) — mitigations applied, firmware rollout planned.

anika: provisional ok. We'll keep watch for 24h for regressions.

maya: closing loop — incident doc link: https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-20260315-AP1-NVME (will add postmortem later).
